title: Sell Mineral Rights in Nebraska
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Nebraska | Royalty Buyer
metaDescription: Own Nebraska minerals with no royalty check coming in, or a small one from the Niobrara/DJ basin edge? We evaluate non-producing and producing interests both.
heroLead: Most of the Nebraska mineral inquiries the royalty desk receives aren't about a check at all, they're about a piece of paper that's never paid anything and an owner trying to figure out if it's worth keeping.
intro: Nebraska sits on the far northeast edge of the DJ Basin and Niobrara play, and that geography matters more here than in most other states the royalty desk reviews. A handful of counties in the southwest corner, Dundy, Chase, Perkins, have seen real drilling tied to the same Niobrara chalk that's productive across the Colorado line. Most of the rest of the state's mineral ownership has never had a well drilled on it and probably never will.

That doesn't make the interest worthless, it just means the conversation is different from a Texas or Oklahoma call. The royalty desk explains plainly which situation you're in before discussing numbers.

sections.heading: Nebraska's Place on the DJ Basin Map
paragraphs: The active edge of Nebraska's oil play sits in Dundy, Chase, and Perkins counties, tied into the same Niobrara and Codell formations that operators have worked hard across the border in Colorado's Wattenberg field. Wells here have been drilled in fits and starts depending on commodity prices and operator focus, so production history is choppier than in a core basin state.

If you're in one of these counties and have an active lease or a check coming, we look at the well's actual production, alongside its location relative to Colorado activity, before putting a number together.

sections.heading: Non-Producing Doesn't Mean Worthless
paragraphs: Plenty of Nebraska mineral owners hold interests, often inherited from grandparents who homesteaded the land, that have never been leased or have sat under an old lease with no drilling. Those interests still have value, tied mostly to the possibility of future leasing activity and any bonus money that comes with it.

That value is lower and more speculative than a producing interest, and any honest buyer needs to say so upfront. We'll tell you if what you're holding is realistically a hold-and-wait situation or something worth cashing out of now.

sections.heading: What a Nebraska Title Search Usually Turns Up
paragraphs: Because so little of the state has seen drilling, a lot of Nebraska mineral records haven't been touched since the original severance or a single estate transfer decades ago. That can mean thin paper trails, which is normal and workable, but it also means we sometimes find gaps that need a courthouse trip in the county seat to sort out.
We handle that research as part of any offer process. You don't need a clean, modern title file for us to get started, you need to know roughly where the property sits and what you believe you own.

sections.heading: Setting Realistic Expectations on a Nebraska Sale
paragraphs: For producing interests in the southwest counties, we price against actual well performance the same way we would anywhere else. For non-producing acreage in the rest of the state, pricing is smaller and reflects speculative leasing potential rather than cash flow, and we say that directly rather than dressing it up.

Some owners decide a modest, certain payment today beats holding paper that may never pay a dime. Others decide to keep waiting. Both are reasonable, and we're not going to push you toward a sale that doesn't make sense for your situation.

faqs.question: Are Nebraska mineral rights worth evaluating if they have never produced a check?
faqs.answer: Possibly, though value depends heavily on location relative to active drilling and any leasing history. We evaluate non-producing acreage differently than producing interests and will tell you honestly where yours likely falls.

faqs.question: Which Nebraska counties have actual oil production?
faqs.answer: The active area sits mostly in Dundy, Chase, and Perkins counties in the state's southwest corner, tied to the DJ Basin Niobrara play that extends from Colorado. Most other Nebraska counties have little to no history of drilling.

faqs.question: Your family inherited mineral rights and nobody knows the legal description. What now?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever documents exist, an old deed, a probate filing, anything with a legal description or county name, and we can usually trace ownership through county records from there.

faqs.question: Should you lease instead of selling your Nebraska minerals?
faqs.answer: If your acreage is in an area seeing active leasing interest, that's worth exploring. If it's outside the productive trend, a lease offer may never come, and selling outright can be the more realistic path to getting value from the property.

faqs.question: How do you value Nebraska mineral rights that have never had a well drilled on them?
faqs.answer: We look at proximity to active Dundy, Chase, and Perkins county drilling, any historical leasing bonuses paid in the surrounding township, and how the play has trended over recent years. It's a smaller, more speculative number than a producing interest, and we explain the reasoning behind it rather than just naming a figure.

faqs.question: Do you need a survey or professional appraisal before selling your Nebraska mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No. We handle the title and production research ourselves as part of preparing an offer, so you don't need to pay for a separate appraisal or survey before talking to us.
